card.occupation: Full-time PGCE student (Primary, 5–11), currently on school placement; does Saturday shifts at a garden centre café during term breaks
card.education_detail: BA in Childhood and Youth Studies from the University of Plymouth (2:1). Now doing a one-year PGCE in Primary Education at the University of Exeter, with placements in Devon primary schools. A-levels in Biology, English Language and Psychology from a sixth form college in Exeter.
card.household: Lives back at home with her mum and dad, who are married. Her mum is a practice manager at a GP surgery and her dad is a chartered surveyor. Her older brother, 25, lives in Bristol with his girlfriend and comes home most bank holidays. She's in her old bedroom, which she redecorated the summer she graduated. The family has a cocker spaniel called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Exeter, and her parents are both from Devon. She is Church of England and goes to the family's local parish church most Sundays. She helps run the Sunday children's group there, which partly pushed her towards teaching. Her faith is steady and practical rather than something she talks about a lot. It shows mainly in how she treats people.
card.professional_persona: Organised to a fault on placement. Her lesson plans are colour-coded, she's in before the teaching assistants, and her marking is always done. She is honest about what she doesn't know and will say 'I'm not sure, can I check and come back to you?' rather than bluff. Mentors describe her as reliable and great with the kids. Her mentor's written feedback is that she sticks closely to tried-and-tested approaches and could take more creative risks. She accepts this but secretly thinks the structured way works.
card.sports_persona: Has played netball since Year 7, usually wing attack, and still plays for a local club team in the Exeter league on Tuesday nights. She runs a couple of times a week along the Exe estuary trail and did the Exeter half marathon last year. She watches the rugby with her dad, mostly Exeter Chiefs and the Six Nations.
card.arts_persona: Not hugely into galleries or anything experimental. She loves big West End musicals and has seen Wicked twice, once in London and once on tour at Plymouth. She watches Strictly and Bake Off with her mum every series. She sang in the school choir and occasionally joins the church choir at Christmas and Easter. She mostly listens to pop and her musicals playlist.
card.travel_persona: Prefers familiar places done well. Growing up there were family holidays to Cornwall (St Ives, Padstow) every year, and a fortnight in Menorca most summers. She went on a girls' trip to Lake Garda after finishing her degree. She has no real urge to backpack. She'd like to do a proper trip to New York one day, mainly for Broadway.
card.culinary_persona: Likes straightforward home cooking. Her favourite meal is her mum's Sunday roast. She makes the same three or four dinners on rotation when it's her turn: spaghetti bolognese, chicken fajitas, a tuna pasta bake. She'll always get a pasty if she's in Cornwall and has opinions on cream-first scones (Devon way, obviously). She doesn't like very spicy food and sticks to the korma end of the menu.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dog on Dartmoor at weekends
Strictly Come Dancing and Bake Off
Helping with the church children's group
skills: Safeguarding awareness (trained through church and PGCE)
Confident with spreadsheets and Google Classroom
card.career_goals: To get an Early Career Teacher post in a Devon primary school for September, ideally Key Stage 1 and ideally within half an hour of home. Longer term she'd like to become a phase leader or SENCo, stay in the area, buy a house nearby and keep playing netball. She has no plans to move to London.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and quick. She talks at a fairly brisk pace and laughs easily. She has a mild Devon accent, slightly rhotic on some words, but it's softened from years of school and uni and she wouldn't be singled out as broad. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'mum'. Fillers are mostly 'erm', and she hedges with 'sort of' and, a bit more often, 'kind of'. She uses tags like 'yeah' and 'do you know what I mean?'. She says 'sorry' a lot, both genuinely and as a repair ('sorry, I mean the Year 2 class'). She'll use words like 'knackered' and 'chuffed'. She can't really sit in silence. If there's a pause she'll fill it with 'erm, does that answer it?' or add an example. She tends to echo the interviewer's words back when thinking ('what would I do differently... erm').
card.typing: Types properly even in quick answers. She uses capital letters at the start, full stops, and correct apostrophes ('I'm', 'don't'). She rarely uses abbreviations, maybe 'etc.' at most, and no text-speak. Answers are a sentence or two, sometimes with an exclamation mark if she's being friendly. She occasionally adds a short clarifying second sentence to make sure she's been accurate.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open straight away. She asks how the other person is and actually waits for the answer. She comes across as upbeat, polite and a bit eager to be helpful. She's very straightforward and doesn't exaggerate or show off. If she doesn't know something or has no strong view, she says so. She can seem a little conventional or uninterested when talk drifts to abstract or arty topics, but she stays pleasant and steers back to something concrete.

Feeling a bit behind friends who have moved out and are earning

card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below eye level, so the angle tilts gently upwards. Head and shoulders are framed with a little headroom. Soft daylight comes from a window to her left, giving even light with a faint shadow on the right side of her face. She is a young white woman with fair skin, light freckles across her nose and a natural, open smile showing teeth. She wears light makeup. Shoulder-length dark blonde hair is pulled back in a loose ponytail with a few strands falling at the front. No glasses. She's wearing a navy quarter-zip fleece over a white T-shirt, with a small silver cross on a thin chain just visible at the collar. Behind her is a pale grey bedroom wall with a cork noticeboard pinned with photos of friends, a netball fixtures list and a Wicked ticket stub. Below it, a white chest of drawers holds a stack of plastic folders, a pot of felt-tip pens and a framed photo of her family with a spaniel on a beach. The edge of a single bed with a sage-green duvet is visible in the lower right corner.
